# What the Mirror Cannot See

*An interactive guide to the sign of a functional equation, the moves that preserve it, and the complete answer to the question "what does the sign know?"*

---

## 1. Eigenvalues in a mirror

Count the points of a variety over $\mathbb{F}_q, \mathbb{F}_{q^2}, \mathbb{F}_{q^3},\dots$ and you find that every count is governed by finitely many complex numbers $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_d$, the eigenvalues of Frobenius (see the [Weil conjectures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weil_conjectures)). Poincaré duality makes the list look the same in a mirror: with $Q = q^w$,

$$\alpha \ \text{is on the list} \iff \frac{Q}{\alpha}\ \text{is on the list (with the same multiplicity).}$$

We call such a list a **duality eigensystem**. Its characteristic polynomial $P(T)=\prod(1-\alpha_i T)$ satisfies a functional equation whose **sign** is
$$\varepsilon = \frac{\alpha_1\cdots\alpha_d}{s^d},\qquad s=\sqrt{Q}.$$

<details><summary>Where does the functional equation come from? (click)</summary>

Substitute $T \mapsto 1/(QT)$:
$$P\!\left(\tfrac{1}{QT}\right)=\prod_i\Bigl(1-\frac{\alpha_i}{QT}\Bigr)=(QT)^{-d}\prod_i(QT-\alpha_i)=(-1)^d(QT)^{-d}\Bigl(\prod_i\alpha_i\Bigr)\prod_i\Bigl(1-\frac{Q}{\alpha_i}T\Bigr).$$
Because $\{Q/\alpha_i\}$ is a permutation of $\{\alpha_i\}$, the last product is $P(T)$ again, which gives $P(1/(QT)) = (-1)^d\,\varepsilon\,Q^{-d/2}T^{-d}P(T)$.
</details>

In units of $\sqrt Q$ (divide every eigenvalue by $s$) the mirror becomes $z\mapsto 1/z$, and only two points stand still: $+1=+\sqrt Q$ and $-1=-\sqrt Q$.

{{visualization:0}}

## 2. The sign is one bit

A genuine mirror pair $\{\beta, Q/\beta\}$ multiplies to $Q=s^2$ and contributes nothing to $\varepsilon$. The fixed points contribute $+1$ (for $+s$) or $-1$ (for $-s$). Hence:

> **Sign formula.** For every duality eigensystem, $\varepsilon = (-1)^{n_-}$, where $n_-$ is the number of eigenvalues equal to $-\sqrt Q$.

<details><summary>Proof sketch: peel off pairs</summary>

Use strong induction on the size. Pick any element $a$. If $a$ is fixed by the mirror, then $a=\pm s$; remove it, and the rest is still mirror-symmetric. Otherwise remove $a$ together with its partner $Q/a$; their product is $s^2$, and neither of them is $-s$. In both cases the induction hypothesis finishes the proof. Mirror symmetry of the remainder follows because the mirror is injective, so applying it commutes with erasing one element.
</details>

The first algorithm computes the sign this way and returns a certificate: the list of pairs it peeled off.

{{algorithm:0}}

## 3. The conjecture: double-minus moves

The sign sees only the parity of $n_-$. Could the invisible rest be generated by simple moves?

- **permute** the eigenvalues;
- **double-minus**: insert or delete a pair $(-\sqrt Q,-\sqrt Q)$;
- **twist** $\alpha\mapsto-\alpha$, which multiplies $\varepsilon$ by $(-1)^d$ and is therefore allowed only in even degree.

All three moves preserve the sign, mirror symmetry, and the parity of the degree. The conjecture claimed the converse: *equal degree and equal sign imply that the systems are related by moves*.

**Try it.** In the workbench below, preset "F₂ vs F₃" loads $[2\sqrt Q,\sqrt Q/2]$ and $[3\sqrt Q,\sqrt Q/3]$. They have the same degree and the same sign. Can the original moves connect them?

{{interactive_demo:0}}

## 4. The core, and the complete classification

Split a system into its fixed-point counts $n_+$, $n_-$ and its **core**, the eigenvalues other than $\pm\sqrt Q$. A double-minus move changes $n_-$ by $2$. A twist negates the core and swaps $n_+$ with $n_-$. Nothing ever changes the core except that global sign.

> **Classification theorem.** Two lists are related by the original moves if and only if
> - *(odd degree)* they have the same core, the same $n_+$, and $n_-$ of the same parity;
> - *(even degree)* they have the same core and the same parities of $n_+$ and $n_-$, **or** opposite cores and swapped parities.

<details><summary>Proof sketch: normal forms and the twist–insert–twist trick</summary>

Every list can be reduced to $[s]^a\,[-s]^b\,C$ with $b\in\{0,1\}$ by deleting $(-s,-s)$ pairs. In even degree, *twist, insert $(-s,-s)$, twist back* inserts a pair $(+s,+s)$:
$$L \to -L \to (-s,-s,-L) \to (s,s,L).$$
So in even degree $a\in\{0,1\}$ as well. Lists with matching invariants reach the same normal form. In the twisted case, twist one of them first.
</details>

{{algorithm:1}}

A consequence is easy to miss: **in a fixed odd degree the moves do nothing beyond permuting.** Equal core, equal $n_+$ and equal degree force equal $n_-$.

## 5. The verdict

> **Exact boundary.** The conjecture holds in degree $d$ if and only if $d\le 1$.

For $d\ge2$ the family $F_n=[n\sqrt Q,\ \sqrt Q/n,\ \sqrt Q,\dots,\sqrt Q]$ for $n=2,3,4,\dots$ consists of eigensystems that all have sign $+1$. Yet $F_n$ and $F_m$ are move-equivalent only when $n=m$, because their cores $\{n\sqrt Q,\sqrt Q/n\}$ differ even up to sign. **A single sign class contains infinitely many move classes.**

<details><summary>Two more subtleties</summary>

- *Core-free, even degree:* if every eigenvalue is $\pm\sqrt Q$ and the degree is even, the conjecture **holds**.
- *Core-free, odd degree:* $[\sqrt Q,\sqrt Q,\sqrt Q]$ and $[\sqrt Q,-\sqrt Q,-\sqrt Q]$ both have sign $+1$, but in odd degree $n_+$ is an exact invariant, so they are **not** related. Use the preset "core-free odd" in the workbench to check this.
</details>

The demo below confirms the classification by brute force over every list of length at most $6$ in a small alphabet, prints the infinite family, and counts the classes inside each sign class.

{{demo:0}}

## 6. The repair: let any mirror pair come and go

The double-minus move inserts one specific mirror pair. Allow **every** mirror pair $\{\beta,Q/\beta\}$ to be inserted and deleted, and no twist is needed:

> **Dual-pair completeness.** Two duality eigensystems of the same degree have the same sign *if and only if* they are related by permutations and insertions or deletions of mirror pairs. This holds in every degree.

The reduction always ends at one of four normal forms:

| normal form | degree parity | sign |
|---|---|---|
| $[\ ]$ | even | $+1$ |
| $[\sqrt Q,-\sqrt Q]$ | even | $-1$ |
| $[\sqrt Q]$ | odd | $+1$ |
| $[-\sqrt Q]$ | odd | $-1$ |

In the workbench, press **reduce to normal form** and watch the sign stay fixed while the system collapses.

{{algorithm:2}}

<details><summary>Why the four forms are distinguished by (degree, sign)</summary>

The core of an eigensystem has even size, because it splits into pairs $\beta\neq Q/\beta$. So $n_+\equiv d-n_- \pmod 2$. If $d$ and the parity of $n_-$ (that is, the sign) are fixed, both parities are fixed, and so is the normal form.
</details>

## 7. What the functional equation sees

It sees the **degree** and the **sign**, and nothing else. Everything else, including the whole continuous family of cores, can be added and removed one mirror pair at a time without the functional equation noticing. The original double-minus moves are strictly weaker: $[2\sqrt Q,\sqrt Q/2]$ and $[3\sqrt Q,\sqrt Q/3]$ are related by one deletion and one insertion of mirror pairs, but by no sequence of the original moves.

Open questions: Can the chain of moves be kept *integral*, with every intermediate system a genuine Weil polynomial? Is the space of cores a symmetric power of a punctured plane modulo $z\mapsto -z$? How do the generators change for symmetric versus alternating pairings? See the Future Directions tab, and the background on [local zeta functions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_zeta_function), the [Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birch_and_Swinnerton-Dyer_conjecture) and [functional equations of L-functions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Functional_equation_(L-function)).

public import Mathlib

/-!
# Duality eigensystems and their sign

We model the eigenvalue data of a pure weight-`w` piece of a Weil cohomology
satisfying Poincaré duality.  Write `Q = q ^ w` and fix a square root `s` of `Q`
(so `s ^ 2 = Q`; for an honest Weil number `s = q ^ (w / 2) > 0`, but all the
algebra below works for any nonzero complex `s`).

* A *duality eigensystem* is a finite list of nonzero complex numbers
  `α₁, …, α_d` (the inverse roots of the characteristic polynomial) which, as a
  multiset, is stable under the duality involution `α ↦ Q / α = s ^ 2 / α`.
* Its *sign* is `ε = (α₁ ⋯ α_d) / s ^ d`; this is the sign appearing in the
  functional equation `P(1 / (Q T)) = ± ε Q^{-d/2} T^{-d} P(T)`.
* The fixed points of the involution are exactly `±s`; we call `-s` the
  *`-Q` fixed points* (the eigenvalue `-√Q`).

The main result of this file is the *sign formula*
`ε = (-1) ^ (number of -Q fixed points)`, proved by peeling off fixed points and
dual pairs one at a time.
-/

@[expose] public section

noncomputable section

namespace DualityMoves

open Multiset

/-- The duality involution `α ↦ Q / α`, written with `Q = s ^ 2`. -/
def dual (s a : ℂ) : ℂ := s ^ 2 / a

/-- A *duality eigensystem* (relative to `s = √Q`): nonzero eigenvalues whose
multiset is stable under `α ↦ s ^ 2 / α`. -/
def IsEigensystem (s : ℂ) (l : List ℂ) : Prop :=
  (∀ a ∈ l, a ≠ 0) ∧ List.Perm (l.map (dual s)) l

/-- The sign of the functional equation: `∏ αᵢ / s ^ d`. -/
noncomputable def sign (s : ℂ) (l : List ℂ) : ℂ := l.prod / s ^ l.length

/-- Number of `-Q` fixed points, i.e. occurrences of the eigenvalue `-s`. -/
def negFix (s : ℂ) (l : List ℂ) : ℕ := l.count (-s)

lemma dual_injective {s : ℂ} (hs : s ≠ 0) : Function.Injective (dual s) := by
  intro a b h
  unfold dual at h
  have hs2 : s ^ 2 ≠ 0 := pow_ne_zero 2 hs
  rw [div_eq_mul_inv, div_eq_mul_inv] at h
  exact inv_injective (mul_left_cancel₀ hs2 h)

lemma dual_dual {s a : ℂ} (hs : s ≠ 0) (ha : a ≠ 0) : dual s (dual s a) = a := by
  unfold dual; field_simp

lemma dual_neg (s a : ℂ) : dual s (-a) = - dual s a := by
  unfold dual; ring

lemma dual_ne_zero {s a : ℂ} (hs : s ≠ 0) (ha : a ≠ 0) : dual s a ≠ 0 := by
  unfold dual; exact div_ne_zero (pow_ne_zero 2 hs) ha

/-- The fixed points of the duality involution are exactly `±s`. -/
lemma dual_eq_self_iff {s a : ℂ} (ha : a ≠ 0) : dual s a = a ↔ a = s ∨ a = -s := by
  unfold dual
  rw [div_eq_iff ha]
  constructor
  · intro h
    have : (a - s) * (a + s) = 0 := by linear_combination -h
    rcases mul_eq_zero.1 this with h1 | h1
    · left; linear_combination h1
    · right; linear_combination h1
  · rintro (rfl | rfl) <;> ring

lemma dual_self_s (s : ℂ) (hs : s ≠ 0) : dual s s = s :=
  (dual_eq_self_iff hs).2 (Or.inl rfl)

lemma dual_self_neg_s (s : ℂ) (hs : s ≠ 0) : dual s (-s) = -s :=
  (dual_eq_self_iff (neg_ne_zero.2 hs)).2 (Or.inr rfl)

/-- Removing one element `a` from a duality-closed multiset: the result is closed
under duality after also removing `dual a`. -/
lemma map_dual_erase {s : ℂ} (hs : s ≠ 0) (M : Multiset ℂ) (hM : M.map (dual s) = M)
    (a : ℂ) : (M.erase a).map (dual s) = M.erase (dual s a) := by
  rw [Multiset.map_erase _ (dual_injective hs), hM]

/-- **Sign formula (multiset form).**  For a duality-closed multiset of nonzero
numbers, `∏ α = (-1) ^ #{α = -s} · s ^ d`. -/
theorem prod_eq_of_dualClosed {s : ℂ} (hs : s ≠ 0) :
    ∀ (M : Multiset ℂ), (∀ a ∈ M, a ≠ 0) → M.map (dual s) = M →
      M.prod = (-1) ^ (M.count (-s)) * s ^ (card M) := by
  intro M
  induction hn : card M using Nat.strong_induction_on generalizing M with
  | _ n ih =>
  intro h0 hd
  rcases Multiset.empty_or_exists_mem M with rfl | ⟨a, haM⟩
  · subst hn; simp
  have ha0 := h0 a haM
  have hsn : s ≠ -s := fun h => hs (by linear_combination h / 2)
  by_cases hfix : dual s a = a
  · -- a is a fixed point: a = s or a = -s
    set M' := M.erase a with hM'
    have hM : M = a ::ₘ M' := (Multiset.cons_erase haM).symm
    have h0' : ∀ b ∈ M', b ≠ 0 := fun b hb => h0 b (Multiset.mem_of_mem_erase hb)
    have hd' : M'.map (dual s) = M' := by
      have := map_dual_erase hs M hd a
      rwa [hfix] at this
    have hcard : card M' + 1 = n := by rw [← hn, hM, Multiset.card_cons]
    have IH := ih (card M') (by omega) M' rfl h0' hd'
    rw [hM, Multiset.prod_cons, IH, ← hcard]
    rcases (dual_eq_self_iff ha0).1 hfix with rfl | rfl
    · rw [Multiset.count_cons_of_ne hsn.symm]; ring
    · rw [Multiset.count_cons_self]; ring
  · -- a is paired with b = dual a ≠ a
    set b := dual s a with hb
    have hbM : b ∈ M := by rw [← hd]; exact Multiset.mem_map_of_mem _ haM
    have hbM' : b ∈ M.erase a := (Multiset.mem_erase_of_ne hfix).2 hbM
    set M'' := (M.erase a).erase b with hM''
    have hM : M = a ::ₘ b ::ₘ M'' := by
      rw [hM'', Multiset.cons_erase hbM', Multiset.cons_erase haM]
    have h0' : ∀ c ∈ M'', c ≠ 0 := fun c hc =>
      h0 c (Multiset.mem_of_mem_erase (Multiset.mem_of_mem_erase hc))
    have hd' : M''.map (dual s) = M'' := by
      rw [hM'', Multiset.map_erase _ (dual_injective hs), map_dual_erase hs M hd a,
        hb, dual_dual hs ha0, Multiset.erase_comm]
    have hcard : card M'' + 2 = n := by rw [← hn, hM]; simp
    have IH := ih (card M'') (by omega) M'' rfl h0' hd'
    have ha_ne : a ≠ -s := fun h => hfix (by rw [hb, h]; exact dual_self_neg_s s hs)
    have hb_ne : b ≠ -s := by
      intro h
      apply ha_ne
      have : dual s b = dual s (-s) := by rw [h]
      rwa [hb, dual_dual hs ha0, dual_self_neg_s s hs] at this
    have hab : a * b = s ^ 2 := by rw [hb]; unfold dual; field_simp
    rw [hM, Multiset.prod_cons, Multiset.prod_cons, ← mul_assoc, hab, IH,
      Multiset.count_cons_of_ne ha_ne.symm, Multiset.count_cons_of_ne hb_ne.symm, ← hcard]
    ring

/-- **Sign formula.**  For every duality eigensystem,
`∏ αᵢ = (-1) ^ (#-Q fixed points) · s ^ d`. -/
theorem prod_eq (s : ℂ) (hs : s ≠ 0) (l : List ℂ) (hl : IsEigensystem s l) :
    l.prod = (-1) ^ negFix s l * s ^ l.length := by
  have hd : (l : Multiset ℂ).map (dual s) = l := by
    rw [Multiset.map_coe]; exact Multiset.coe_eq_coe.2 hl.2
  have := prod_eq_of_dualClosed hs (l : Multiset ℂ) (fun a ha => hl.1 a ha) hd
  simpa [negFix] using this

/-- **Sign formula.**  The sign of a duality eigensystem is
`(-1) ^ (number of -Q fixed points)`. -/
theorem sign_eq (s : ℂ) (hs : s ≠ 0) (l : List ℂ) (hl : IsEigensystem s l) :
    sign s l = (-1) ^ negFix s l := by
  rw [sign, prod_eq s hs l hl, mul_div_assoc, div_self (pow_ne_zero _ hs), mul_one]

/-- Two duality eigensystems have the same sign iff their numbers of `-Q` fixed
points have the same parity (the "proved converse" in sign-parity form). -/
theorem sign_eq_sign_iff (s : ℂ) (hs : s ≠ 0) (l l' : List ℂ)
    (hl : IsEigensystem s l) (hl' : IsEigensystem s l') :
    sign s l = sign s l' ↔ negFix s l % 2 = negFix s l' % 2 := by
  rw [sign_eq s hs l hl, sign_eq s hs l' hl']
  rcases Nat.even_or_odd (negFix s l) with h1 | h1 <;>
    rcases Nat.even_or_odd (negFix s l') with h2 | h2 <;>
    simp [h1.neg_one_pow, h2.neg_one_pow, Nat.even_iff.1, Nat.odd_iff.1, h1, h2] <;>
    norm_num

end DualityMoves

end

module

public import Catalog.Geometry.DualityMoves.Basic

/-!
# The move relation on eigensystems

We formalise the moves of the conjecture as an inductive relation on lists of
eigenvalues:

* `perm`       — reorder the eigenvalues;
* `insertPair` — insert a pair of `-Q` fixed points `-s, -s` (and, through
  `symm`, delete such a pair);
* `twist`      — the quadratic twist `α ↦ -α` (the only twists preserving
  duality are by `±1`); it changes the sign by `(-1)^d`, so it is a
  sign-preserving move exactly in even degree, which is when we allow it;
* `symm`, `trans` — the relation is the equivalence relation generated.

Main results:
* `Moves.sign_eq`        — the moves preserve the sign (sign invariance);
* `Moves.isEigensystem`  — the moves preserve being a duality eigensystem;
* `Moves.length_mod_two` — degree parity is preserved;
* `Moves.relR`, `Moves.relO` — the finer invariants preserved by the moves.
-/

@[expose] public section

noncomputable section

namespace DualityMoves

/-- The move relation generated by permutations, insertion/deletion of a pair
of `-Q` fixed points, and (sign-preserving, i.e. even-degree) quadratic twists. -/
inductive Moves (s : ℂ) : List ℂ → List ℂ → Prop
  | perm {l l' : List ℂ} : l.Perm l' → Moves s l l'
  | insertPair (l : List ℂ) : Moves s l (-s :: -s :: l)
  | twist (l : List ℂ) : Even l.length → Moves s l (l.map Neg.neg)
  | symm {l l' : List ℂ} : Moves s l l' → Moves s l' l
  | trans {l l' l'' : List ℂ} : Moves s l l' → Moves s l' l'' → Moves s l l''

/-- The *core* of an eigenvalue list: the eigenvalues that are not fixed by
duality (everything except `±s`). -/
def coreList (s : ℂ) (l : List ℂ) : List ℂ := l.filter (fun a => decide (a ≠ s ∧ a ≠ -s))

/-- The core as a multiset (order forgotten). -/
def core (s : ℂ) (l : List ℂ) : Multiset ℂ := (coreList s l : Multiset ℂ)

lemma count_coreList (s x : ℂ) (l : List ℂ) :
    (coreList s l).count x = if x ≠ s ∧ x ≠ -s then l.count x else 0 := by
  unfold coreList
  split_ifs with h
  · exact List.count_filter (by simpa using h)
  · apply List.count_eq_zero_of_not_mem
    intro hx
    rw [List.mem_filter] at hx
    exact h (by simpa using hx.2)

lemma core_eq_iff (s : ℂ) (l l' : List ℂ) :
    core s l = core s l' ↔ ∀ x, x ≠ s → x ≠ -s → l.count x = l'.count x := by
  unfold core
  rw [Multiset.coe_eq_coe, List.perm_iff_count]
  constructor
  · intro h x h1 h2
    have := h x
    rwa [count_coreList, count_coreList, if_pos ⟨h1, h2⟩, if_pos ⟨h1, h2⟩] at this
  · intro h x
    rw [count_coreList, count_coreList]
    split_ifs with h'
    · exact h x h'.1 h'.2
    · rfl

lemma count_map_neg (x : ℂ) (l : List ℂ) : (l.map Neg.neg).count x = l.count (-x) := by
  have := List.count_map_of_injective l Neg.neg neg_injective (-x)
  simpa using this

lemma core_map_neg (s : ℂ) (l : List ℂ) :
    core s (l.map Neg.neg) = (core s l).map Neg.neg := by
  unfold core
  rw [Multiset.map_coe, Multiset.coe_eq_coe, List.perm_iff_count]
  intro x
  rw [count_coreList, count_map_neg, count_map_neg, count_coreList]
  have : (x ≠ s ∧ x ≠ -s) ↔ (-x ≠ s ∧ -x ≠ -s) := by
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩
      exact ⟨fun h => h2 (by linear_combination -h), fun h => h1 (by linear_combination -h)⟩
    · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩
      exact ⟨fun h => h2 (by linear_combination -h), fun h => h1 (by linear_combination -h)⟩
  simp only [this]

/-! ### Invariants -/

/-- The invariant preserved by all moves: the core is preserved up to the
twist `α ↦ -α`, and the parities of the numbers of `+Q` and `-Q` fixed points
are preserved (swapped, together with negating the core, by a twist). -/
def RelR (s : ℂ) (l l' : List ℂ) : Prop :=
  ((∀ x, x ≠ s → x ≠ -s → l'.count x = l.count x) ∧
      l'.count s % 2 = l.count s % 2 ∧ l'.count (-s) % 2 = l.count (-s) % 2) ∨
  ((∀ x, x ≠ s → x ≠ -s → l'.count x = l.count (-x)) ∧
      l'.count s % 2 = l.count (-s) % 2 ∧ l'.count (-s) % 2 = l.count s % 2)

/-- The invariant preserved by moves out of an odd-degree list: the core and the
exact number of `+Q` fixed points are preserved, and the number of `-Q` fixed
points is preserved modulo `2`. -/
def RelO (s : ℂ) (l l' : List ℂ) : Prop :=
  (∀ x, x ≠ s → x ≠ -s → l'.count x = l.count x) ∧
    l'.count s = l.count s ∧ l'.count (-s) % 2 = l.count (-s) % 2

lemma neg_ne_pm {s x : ℂ} (h1 : x ≠ s) (h2 : x ≠ -s) : -x ≠ s ∧ -x ≠ -s :=
  ⟨fun h => h2 (by linear_combination -h), fun h => h1 (by linear_combination -h)⟩

lemma relR_refl (s : ℂ) (l : List ℂ) : RelR s l l := Or.inl ⟨fun _ _ _ => rfl, rfl, rfl⟩

lemma relR_symm {s : ℂ} {l l' : List ℂ} (h : RelR s l l') : RelR s l' l := by
  rcases h with ⟨h1, h2, h3⟩ | ⟨h1, h2, h3⟩
  · exact Or.inl ⟨fun x a b => (h1 x a b).symm, h2.symm, h3.symm⟩
  · refine Or.inr ⟨fun x a b => ?_, h3.symm, h2.symm⟩
    obtain ⟨a', b'⟩ := neg_ne_pm a b
    rw [h1 (-x) a' b', neg_neg]

lemma relR_trans {s : ℂ} {l l' l'' : List ℂ} (h : RelR s l l') (h' : RelR s l' l'') :
    RelR s l l'' := by
  rcases h with ⟨h1, h2, h3⟩ | ⟨h1, h2, h3⟩ <;> rcases h' with ⟨k1, k2, k3⟩ | ⟨k1, k2, k3⟩
  · exact Or.inl ⟨fun x a b => by rw [k1 x a b, h1 x a b], by omega, by omega⟩
  · refine Or.inr ⟨fun x a b => ?_, by omega, by omega⟩
    obtain ⟨a', b'⟩ := neg_ne_pm a b
    rw [k1 x a b, h1 (-x) a' b']
  · exact Or.inr ⟨fun x a b => by rw [k1 x a b, h1 x a b], by omega, by omega⟩
  · refine Or.inl ⟨fun x a b => ?_, by omega, by omega⟩
    obtain ⟨a', b'⟩ := neg_ne_pm a b
    rw [k1 x a b, h1 (-x) a' b', neg_neg]

lemma relO_symm {s : ℂ} {l l' : List ℂ} (h : RelO s l l') : RelO s l' l :=
  ⟨fun x a b => (h.1 x a b).symm, h.2.1.symm, h.2.2.symm⟩

lemma relO_trans {s : ℂ} {l l' l'' : List ℂ} (h : RelO s l l') (h' : RelO s l' l'') :
    RelO s l l'' :=
  ⟨fun x a b => by rw [h'.1 x a b, h.1 x a b], by rw [h'.2.1, h.2.1], by rw [h'.2.2, h.2.2]⟩

lemma count_pair (s x : ℂ) (l : List ℂ) :
    (-s :: -s :: l).count x = l.count x + if x = -s then 2 else 0 := by
  by_cases h : x = -s
  · subst h; simp
  · rw [List.count_cons, List.count_cons]
    simp [Ne.symm h, h]

/-- Moves preserve the parity of the degree. -/
theorem Moves.length_mod_two {s : ℂ} {l l' : List ℂ} (h : Moves s l l') :
    l.length % 2 = l'.length % 2 := by
  induction h with
  | perm hp => rw [hp.length_eq]
  | insertPair l => simp only [List.length_cons]; omega
  | twist l _ => simp
  | symm _ ih => exact ih.symm
  | trans _ _ ih1 ih2 => exact ih1.trans ih2

/-- All moves preserve the invariant `RelR`. -/
theorem Moves.relR {s : ℂ} (hs : s ≠ 0) {l l' : List ℂ} (h : Moves s l l') : RelR s l l' := by
  have hsn : s ≠ -s := fun h => hs (by linear_combination h / 2)
  induction h with
  | perm hp =>
    have := List.perm_iff_count.1 hp
    exact Or.inl ⟨fun x _ _ => (this x).symm, by rw [this], by rw [this]⟩
  | insertPair l =>
    refine Or.inl ⟨fun x _ b => ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · rw [count_pair, if_neg b, add_zero]
    · rw [count_pair, if_neg hsn, add_zero]
    · rw [count_pair, if_pos rfl]; omega
  | twist l _ =>
    refine Or.inr ⟨fun x _ _ => count_map_neg x l, ?_, ?_⟩
    · rw [count_map_neg]
    · rw [count_map_neg, neg_neg]
  | symm _ ih => exact relR_symm ih
  | trans _ _ ih1 ih2 => exact relR_trans ih1 ih2

/-- Moves out of an odd-degree list preserve the finer invariant `RelO`. -/
theorem Moves.relO {s : ℂ} (hs : s ≠ 0) {l l' : List ℂ} (h : Moves s l l') :
    l.length % 2 = 1 → RelO s l l' := by
  have hsn : s ≠ -s := fun h => hs (by linear_combination h / 2)
  induction h with
  | perm hp =>
    intro _
    have := List.perm_iff_count.1 hp
    exact ⟨fun x _ _ => (this x).symm, by rw [this], by rw [this]⟩
  | insertPair l =>
    intro _
    refine ⟨fun x _ b => ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · rw [count_pair, if_neg b, add_zero]
    · rw [count_pair, if_neg hsn, add_zero]
    · rw [count_pair, if_pos rfl]; omega
  | twist l he =>
    intro ho
    exact absurd ho (by rw [Nat.even_iff.1 he]; omega)
  | symm h ih =>
    intro ho
    exact relO_symm (ih (by rw [h.length_mod_two]; exact ho))
  | trans h1 _ ih1 ih2 =>
    intro ho
    exact relO_trans (ih1 ho) (ih2 (by rw [← h1.length_mod_two]; exact ho))

lemma prod_map_neg (l : List ℂ) : (l.map Neg.neg).prod = (-1) ^ l.length * l.prod := by
  induction l with
  | nil => simp
  | cons a t ih =>
    simp only [List.map_cons, List.prod_cons, List.length_cons, ih]
    ring

/-- **Sign invariance.**  Every move preserves the sign `∏ αᵢ / s ^ d`
(this holds for arbitrary eigenvalue lists, not only eigensystems). -/
theorem Moves.sign_eq {s : ℂ} (hs : s ≠ 0) {l l' : List ℂ} (h : Moves s l l') :
    sign s l = sign s l' := by
  induction h with
  | perm hp => unfold sign; rw [hp.prod_eq, hp.length_eq]
  | insertPair l =>
    unfold sign
    simp only [List.prod_cons, List.length_cons]
    field_simp
    ring
  | twist l he =>
    unfold sign
    rw [List.length_map, prod_map_neg, he.neg_one_pow, one_mul]
  | symm _ ih => exact ih.symm
  | trans _ _ ih1 ih2 => exact ih1.trans ih2

/-- Moves preserve being a duality eigensystem. -/
theorem Moves.isEigensystem {s : ℂ} (hs : s ≠ 0) {l l' : List ℂ} (h : Moves s l l') :
    IsEigensystem s l ↔ IsEigensystem s l' := by
  induction h with
  | perm hp =>
    unfold IsEigensystem
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨h0, hd⟩
      exact ⟨fun a ha => h0 a (hp.symm.mem_iff.1 ha), ((hp.map _).symm.trans hd).trans hp⟩
    · rintro ⟨h0, hd⟩
      exact ⟨fun a ha => h0 a (hp.mem_iff.1 ha), ((hp.map _).trans hd).trans hp.symm⟩
  | insertPair l =>
    unfold IsEigensystem
    have hn : -s ≠ 0 := neg_ne_zero.2 hs
    simp only [List.mem_cons, List.map_cons, dual_self_neg_s s hs]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨h0, hd⟩
      exact ⟨by rintro a (rfl | rfl | ha) <;> [exact hn; exact hn; exact h0 a ha],
        (hd.cons _).cons _⟩
    · rintro ⟨h0, hd⟩
      exact ⟨fun a ha => h0 a (Or.inr (Or.inr ha)), (hd.cons_inv).cons_inv⟩
  | twist l _ =>
    unfold IsEigensystem
    have hmap : (l.map Neg.neg).map (dual s) = ((l.map (dual s)).map Neg.neg) := by
      simp [List.map_map, Function.comp_def, dual_neg]
    rw [hmap]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨h0, hd⟩
      refine ⟨fun a ha => ?_, hd.map _⟩
      obtain ⟨b, hb, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.1 ha
      exact neg_ne_zero.2 (h0 b hb)
    · rintro ⟨h0, hd⟩
      refine ⟨fun a ha => ?_, ?_⟩
      · exact neg_ne_zero.1 (h0 (-a) (List.mem_map.2 ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩))
      · have := hd.map Neg.neg
        simpa [List.map_map, Function.comp_def] using this
  | symm _ ih => exact ih.symm
  | trans _ _ ih1 ih2 => exact ih1.trans ih2

end DualityMoves

module

public import Catalog.Geometry.DualityMoves.Moves

/-!
# Complete classification of eigenvalue lists up to the moves

We show that the invariants `RelO` (odd degree) and `RelR` (even degree) found
in `Moves.lean` are *complete*: two lists are related by the moves exactly when
these invariants agree.  The proof is a normal-form argument: every list is
move-equivalent to

  `nf a b C = [s, …, s] ++ [-s, …, -s] ++ C`   (`a` copies of `s`, `b` of `-s`)

where `C` is its core, `b ∈ {0, 1}`, and in even degree also `a ∈ {0, 1}`
(even-degree twists let one cancel pairs of `+Q` fixed points as well).
-/

@[expose] public section

noncomputable section

namespace DualityMoves

/-- The normal form `[s]^a ++ [-s]^b ++ C`. -/
def nf (s : ℂ) (a b : ℕ) (C : List ℂ) : List ℂ :=
  List.replicate a s ++ List.replicate b (-s) ++ C

lemma moves_of_count {s : ℂ} {l l' : List ℂ} (h : ∀ x, l.count x = l'.count x) :
    Moves s l l' := Moves.perm (List.perm_iff_count.2 h)

lemma Moves.refl' (s : ℂ) (l : List ℂ) : Moves s l l := Moves.perm (List.Perm.refl l)

/-- Deleting `k` pairs of `-Q` fixed points. -/
lemma negPairs (s : ℂ) (k : ℕ) : ∀ (l l' : List ℂ),
    (∀ x, x ≠ -s → l.count x = l'.count x) → l.count (-s) = l'.count (-s) + 2 * k →
      Moves s l l' := by
  induction k with
  | zero =>
    intro l l' h1 h2
    apply moves_of_count
    intro x
    by_cases hx : x = -s
    · subst hx; simpa using h2
    · exact h1 x hx
  | succ k ih =>
    intro l l' h1 h2
    refine Moves.trans (ih l (-s :: -s :: l') ?_ ?_) (Moves.symm (Moves.insertPair l'))
    · intro x hx; rw [count_pair, if_neg hx, add_zero]; exact h1 x hx
    · rw [count_pair, if_pos rfl]; omega

/-- In even degree one can also insert a pair of `+Q` fixed points: twist,
insert a `-Q` pair, twist back. -/
lemma posInsert (s : ℂ) (l : List ℂ) (he : Even l.length) : Moves s l (s :: s :: l) := by
  have h1 := Moves.twist (s := s) l he
  have h2 := Moves.insertPair (s := s) (l.map Neg.neg)
  have he' : Even (-s :: -s :: l.map Neg.neg).length := by
    simp only [List.length_cons, List.length_map]
    rw [Nat.even_iff] at he ⊢; omega
  have h3 := Moves.twist (s := s) _ he'
  have : (-s :: -s :: l.map Neg.neg).map Neg.neg = s :: s :: l := by
    simp [List.map_map]
  rw [this] at h3
  exact h1.trans (h2.trans h3)

/-- Deleting `k` pairs of `+Q` fixed points in even degree. -/
lemma posPairs (s : ℂ) (hs : s ≠ 0) (k : ℕ) : ∀ (l l' : List ℂ), Even l'.length →
    (∀ x, x ≠ s → l.count x = l'.count x) → l.count s = l'.count s + 2 * k →
      Moves s l l' := by
  have hsn : -s ≠ s := fun h => hs (by linear_combination -h / 2)
  induction k with
  | zero =>
    intro l l' _ h1 h2
    apply moves_of_count
    intro x
    by_cases hx : x = s
    · subst hx; simpa using h2
    · exact h1 x hx
  | succ k ih =>
    intro l l' he h1 h2
    have hcs : ∀ x, (s :: s :: l').count x = l'.count x + if x = s then 2 else 0 := by
      intro x
      by_cases h : x = s
      · subst h; simp
      · rw [List.count_cons, List.count_cons]; simp [Ne.symm h, h]
    refine Moves.trans (ih l (s :: s :: l') ?_ ?_ ?_) (Moves.symm (posInsert s l' he))
    · simp only [List.length_cons]; rw [Nat.even_iff] at he ⊢; omega
    · intro x hx; rw [hcs, if_neg hx, add_zero]; exact h1 x hx
    · rw [hcs, if_pos rfl]; omega

lemma count_nf (s : ℂ) (hs : s ≠ 0) (a b : ℕ) (C : List ℂ) (x : ℂ) :
    (nf s a b C).count x = (if x = s then a else 0) + (if x = -s then b else 0) + C.count x := by
  have hsn : s ≠ -s := fun h => hs (by linear_combination h / 2)
  unfold nf
  rw [List.count_append, List.count_append, List.count_replicate, List.count_replicate]
  have e1 : (s = x) ↔ (x = s) := eq_comm
  have e2 : (-s = x) ↔ (x = -s) := eq_comm
  simp only [beq_iff_eq, e1, e2]

/-- Every list is a permutation of its normal form `[s]^a ++ [-s]^b ++ core`. -/
lemma perm_nf (s : ℂ) (hs : s ≠ 0) (l : List ℂ) :
    l.Perm (nf s (l.count s) (l.count (-s)) (coreList s l)) := by
  have hsn : s ≠ -s := fun h => hs (by linear_combination h / 2)
  rw [List.perm_iff_count]
  intro x
  rw [count_nf s hs, count_coreList]
  by_cases h1 : x = s
  · rw [if_pos h1, if_neg (by rw [h1]; exact hsn), if_neg (fun h => h.1 h1), h1]; simp
  · by_cases h2 : x = -s
    · rw [if_neg h1, if_pos h2, if_neg (fun h => h.2 h2), h2]; simp
    · rw [if_neg h1, if_neg h2, if_pos ⟨h1, h2⟩]; simp

lemma length_eq_counts (s : ℂ) (hs : s ≠ 0) (l : List ℂ) :
    l.length = l.count s + l.count (-s) + (coreList s l).length := by
  rw [(perm_nf s hs l).length_eq]
  simp only [nf, List.length_append, List.length_replicate]

/-- Odd-degree (in fact any-degree) reduction: cancel pairs of `-Q` fixed points. -/
lemma reduce_neg (s : ℂ) (hs : s ≠ 0) (l : List ℂ) :
    Moves s l (nf s (l.count s) (l.count (-s) % 2) (coreList s l)) := by
  have hsn : s ≠ -s := fun h => hs (by linear_combination h / 2)
  refine (Moves.perm (perm_nf s hs l)).trans (negPairs s (l.count (-s) / 2) _ _ ?_ ?_)
  · intro x hx
    rw [count_nf s hs, count_nf s hs, if_neg hx, if_neg hx]
  · rw [count_nf s hs, count_nf s hs, if_neg hsn.symm, if_pos rfl, if_pos rfl]
    omega

/-- Even-degree reduction: cancel pairs of both kinds of fixed points. -/
lemma reduce_even (s : ℂ) (hs : s ≠ 0) (l : List ℂ) (he : l.length % 2 = 0) :
    Moves s l (nf s (l.count s % 2) (l.count (-s) % 2) (coreList s l)) := by
  have hsn : s ≠ -s := fun h => hs (by linear_combination h / 2)
  refine (reduce_neg s hs l).trans (posPairs s hs (l.count s / 2) _ _ ?_ ?_ ?_)
  · have := length_eq_counts s hs l
    rw [Nat.even_iff]; simp only [nf, List.length_append, List.length_replicate]
    omega
  · intro x hx
    rw [count_nf s hs, count_nf s hs, if_neg hx, if_neg hx]
  · simp only [count_nf s hs, if_neg hsn, if_true]
    omega

lemma coreList_perm {s : ℂ} {l l' : List ℂ}
    (h : ∀ x, x ≠ s → x ≠ -s → l'.count x = l.count x) : (coreList s l).Perm (coreList s l') := by
  rw [List.perm_iff_count]
  intro x
  rw [count_coreList, count_coreList]
  split_ifs with h'
  · exact (h x h'.1 h'.2).symm
  · rfl

lemma nf_perm (s : ℂ) (a b : ℕ) {C C' : List ℂ} (h : C.Perm C') :
    Moves s (nf s a b C) (nf s a b C') := Moves.perm (List.Perm.append_left _ h)

/-- Completeness, first branch of `RelR`, in even degree. -/
lemma complete_even_same (s : ℂ) (hs : s ≠ 0) (l l' : List ℂ) (he : l.length % 2 = 0)
    (h1 : ∀ x, x ≠ s → x ≠ -s → l'.count x = l.count x)
    (h2 : l'.count s % 2 = l.count s % 2) (h3 : l'.count (-s) % 2 = l.count (-s) % 2) :
    Moves s l l' := by
  have hC := coreList_perm h1
  have he' : l'.length % 2 = 0 := by
    have e1 := length_eq_counts s hs l
    have e2 := length_eq_counts s hs l'
    have e3 := hC.length_eq
    omega
  have r1 := reduce_even s hs l he
  have r2 := reduce_even s hs l' he'
  rw [h2, h3] at r2
  exact r1.trans ((nf_perm s _ _ hC).trans r2.symm)

/-- **Complete classification of the move relation.**  Two eigenvalue lists are
related by permutations, insertions/deletions of pairs of `-Q` fixed points and
even-degree quadratic twists iff
* (odd degree) they have the same core, the same number of `+Q` fixed points and
  the same parity of the number of `-Q` fixed points; or
* (even degree) the invariant `RelR` holds: same core and same fixed-point
  parities, or negated core and swapped fixed-point parities. -/
theorem moves_iff (s : ℂ) (hs : s ≠ 0) (l l' : List ℂ) :
    Moves s l l' ↔
      (l.length % 2 = 1 ∧ RelO s l l') ∨ (l.length % 2 = 0 ∧ RelR s l l') := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    rcases Nat.mod_two_eq_zero_or_one l.length with he | ho
    · exact Or.inr ⟨he, h.relR hs⟩
    · exact Or.inl ⟨ho, h.relO hs ho⟩
  · rintro (⟨_, h1, h2, h3⟩ | ⟨he, hR⟩)
    · have r1 := reduce_neg s hs l
      have r2 := reduce_neg s hs l'
      rw [h2, h3] at r2
      exact r1.trans ((nf_perm s _ _ (coreList_perm h1)).trans r2.symm)
    · rcases hR with ⟨h1, h2, h3⟩ | ⟨h1, h2, h3⟩
      · exact complete_even_same s hs l l' he h1 h2 h3
      · -- twist `l'` first
        have he' : Even l'.length := by
          have e1 := length_eq_counts s hs l
          have e2 := length_eq_counts s hs l'
          have hC : (coreList s (l.map Neg.neg)).Perm (coreList s l') := by
            apply coreList_perm
            intro x a b
            rw [h1 x a b, count_map_neg]
          have e3 := hC.length_eq
          have e4 : (coreList s (l.map Neg.neg)).length = (coreList s l).length := by
            have := congrArg Multiset.card (core_map_neg s l)
            simpa [core] using this
          rw [Nat.even_iff]; omega
        refine Moves.trans ?_ (Moves.symm (Moves.twist l' he'))
        apply complete_even_same s hs l _ he
        · intro x a b
          obtain ⟨a', b'⟩ := neg_ne_pm a b
          rw [count_map_neg, h1 (-x) a' b', neg_neg]
        · rw [count_map_neg]; exact h3
        · rw [count_map_neg, neg_neg]; exact h2

/-- The classification restated with the core multiset. -/
theorem moves_iff_core (s : ℂ) (hs : s ≠ 0) (l l' : List ℂ) :
    Moves s l l' ↔
      (l.length % 2 = 1 ∧ core s l' = core s l ∧ l'.count s = l.count s ∧
          negFix s l' % 2 = negFix s l % 2) ∨
      (l.length % 2 = 0 ∧
        ((core s l' = core s l ∧ l'.count s % 2 = l.count s % 2 ∧
            negFix s l' % 2 = negFix s l % 2) ∨
         (core s l' = (core s l).map Neg.neg ∧ l'.count s % 2 = negFix s l % 2 ∧
            negFix s l' % 2 = l.count s % 2))) := by
  rw [moves_iff s hs, RelO, RelR, ← core_map_neg, core_eq_iff, core_eq_iff]
  simp only [negFix, count_map_neg]

end DualityMoves

end

module

public import Catalog.Geometry.DualityMoves.Classification

/-!
# Verdict on the double-minus-move conjecture

*Conjecture.*  Two duality eigensystems of the same degree (and weight) have the
same sign iff they are related by twists, permutations and insertions/deletions
of pairs of `-Q` fixed points.

* The "if" direction is true in every degree: `Moves.sign_eq`.
* The "only if" direction (completeness) holds in degree `d` **iff `d ≤ 1`**
  (`conjectureInDegree_iff`).  For every `d ≥ 2` the eigensystems
  `[n s, s/n, s, …, s]` with `n = 2, 3, 4, …` all have sign `+1` but are pairwise
  not move-equivalent (`fam_moves_iff`), so a single sign class contains
  infinitely many move classes: the core (the non-fixed eigenvalues, up to the
  twist `α ↦ -α`) is a finer invariant than the fixed-point parity, and by
  `moves_iff_core` it is, together with fixed-point counts, the *complete*
  invariant.
* Completeness does hold for *core-free* (all eigenvalues `±√Q`) eigensystems of
  even degree (`complete_coreFree_even`), and fails for core-free ones of odd
  degree `≥ 3` (`coreFree_odd_counterexample`).
-/

@[expose] public section

noncomputable section

namespace DualityMoves

/-- Completeness of the moves in degree `d`: equal sign implies move-equivalence. -/
def ConjectureInDegree (s : ℂ) (d : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ l l' : List ℂ, IsEigensystem s l → IsEigensystem s l' → l.length = d → l'.length = d →
    sign s l = sign s l' → Moves s l l'

/-- The test family `[n s, s / n, s, …, s]` (`k` trailing copies of `s`). -/
def fam (s : ℂ) (n k : ℕ) : List ℂ := (n : ℂ) * s :: s / n :: List.replicate k s

section Arith

variable {s : ℂ} (hs : s ≠ 0)
include hs

lemma natMul_ne_s {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : (n : ℂ) * s ≠ s := by
  intro h
  have : ((n : ℂ) - 1) * s = 0 := by linear_combination h
  rcases mul_eq_zero.1 this with h1 | h1
  · have : (n : ℂ) = (1 : ℕ) := by push_cast; linear_combination h1
    have := Nat.cast_injective this; omega
  · exact hs h1

lemma natMul_ne_neg_s {n : ℕ} : (n : ℂ) * s ≠ -s := by
  intro h
  have : ((n : ℂ) + 1) * s = 0 := by linear_combination h
  rcases mul_eq_zero.1 this with h1 | h1
  · have : ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℂ) = (0 : ℕ) := by push_cast; linear_combination h1
    have := Nat.cast_injective this; omega
  · exact hs h1

lemma natMul_ne_div {n m : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hm : 2 ≤ m) : (n : ℂ) * s ≠ s / m := by
  intro h
  have hm0 : (m : ℂ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast (show m ≠ 0 by omega)
  rw [eq_div_iff hm0] at h
  have : ((n : ℂ) * m - 1) * s = 0 := by linear_combination h
  rcases mul_eq_zero.1 this with h1 | h1
  · have : ((n * m : ℕ) : ℂ) = (1 : ℕ) := by push_cast; linear_combination h1
    have := Nat.cast_injective this
    nlinarith
  · exact hs h1

lemma negNatMul_ne_div {n m : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) : -((n : ℂ) * s) ≠ s / m := by
  intro h
  have hm0 : (m : ℂ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast (show m ≠ 0 by omega)
  rw [eq_div_iff hm0] at h
  have : ((n : ℂ) * m + 1) * s = 0 := by linear_combination -h
  rcases mul_eq_zero.1 this with h1 | h1
  · have : ((n * m + 1 : ℕ) : ℂ) = (0 : ℕ) := by push_cast; linear_combination h1
    have := Nat.cast_injective this; omega
  · exact hs h1

lemma natMul_inj {n m : ℕ} (h : (n : ℂ) * s = (m : ℂ) * s) : n = m := by
  exact_mod_cast mul_right_cancel₀ hs h

lemma negNatMul_ne_natMul {n m : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : -((n : ℂ) * s) ≠ (m : ℂ) * s := by
  intro h
  have : (((n + m : ℕ) : ℂ)) * s = 0 := by push_cast; linear_combination -h
  rcases mul_eq_zero.1 this with h1 | h1
  · have := Nat.cast_injective (h1.trans (Nat.cast_zero).symm); omega
  · exact hs h1

lemma div_ne_s {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : s / n ≠ s := by
  intro h
  have hn0 : (n : ℂ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast (show n ≠ 0 by omega)
  apply natMul_ne_s hs hn
  rw [div_eq_iff hn0] at h; linear_combination -h

lemma div_ne_neg_s {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : s / n ≠ -s := by
  intro h
  have hn0 : (n : ℂ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast (show n ≠ 0 by omega)
  apply natMul_ne_neg_s hs (n := n)
  rw [div_eq_iff hn0] at h; linear_combination h

end Arith

/-- The test family consists of duality eigensystems. -/
lemma fam_isEigensystem (s : ℂ) (hs : s ≠ 0) (n k : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    IsEigensystem s (fam s n k) := by
  have hn0 : (n : ℂ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast (show n ≠ 0 by omega)
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · intro a ha
    simp only [fam, List.mem_cons, List.mem_replicate] at ha
    rcases ha with rfl | rfl | ⟨_, rfl⟩
    · exact mul_ne_zero hn0 hs
    · exact div_ne_zero hs hn0
    · exact hs
  · have h1 : dual s ((n : ℂ) * s) = s / n := by unfold dual; field_simp
    have h2 : dual s (s / n) = (n : ℂ) * s := by unfold dual; field_simp
    have h3 : (List.replicate k s).map (dual s) = List.replicate k s := by
      rw [List.map_replicate, dual_self_s s hs]
    simp only [fam, List.map_cons, h1, h2, h3]
    exact List.Perm.swap _ _ _

/-- Every member of the test family has sign `+1`. -/
lemma fam_sign (s : ℂ) (hs : s ≠ 0) (n k : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : sign s (fam s n k) = 1 := by
  rw [sign_eq s hs _ (fam_isEigensystem s hs n k hn)]
  have hsn : s ≠ -s := fun h => hs (by linear_combination h / 2)
  have : negFix s (fam s n k) = 0 := by
    unfold negFix fam
    apply List.count_eq_zero_of_not_mem
    simp only [List.mem_cons, List.mem_replicate, not_or]
    exact ⟨(natMul_ne_neg_s hs).symm, (div_ne_neg_s hs hn).symm, fun h => hsn h.2.symm⟩
  rw [this, pow_zero]

/-- **Finer invariant.**  Members of the test family (same degree `k + 2`, same
sign `+1`) are move-equivalent only when they coincide. -/
theorem fam_moves_iff (s : ℂ) (hs : s ≠ 0) (n m k : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hm : 2 ≤ m) :
    Moves s (fam s n k) (fam s m k) ↔ n = m := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    have hx1 := natMul_ne_s hs hn
    have hx2 := natMul_ne_neg_s hs (n := n)
    obtain ⟨hy1, hy2⟩ := neg_ne_pm hx1 hx2
    have hpos : 0 < (fam s n k).count ((n : ℂ) * s) := by
      rw [List.count_pos_iff]; simp [fam]
    rcases h.relR hs with ⟨h1, -, -⟩ | ⟨h1, -, -⟩
    · have := h1 _ hx1 hx2
      rw [← this, List.count_pos_iff] at hpos
      simp only [fam, List.mem_cons, List.mem_replicate] at hpos
      rcases hpos with h' | h' | ⟨_, h'⟩
      · exact natMul_inj hs h'
      · exact absurd h' (natMul_ne_div hs hn hm)
      · exact absurd h' hx1
    · have := h1 _ hy1 hy2
      rw [neg_neg] at this
      rw [← this, List.count_pos_iff] at hpos
      simp only [fam, List.mem_cons, List.mem_replicate] at hpos
      rcases hpos with h' | h' | ⟨_, h'⟩
      · exact absurd h' (negNatMul_ne_natMul hs hn)
      · exact absurd h' (negNatMul_ne_div hs hm)
      · exact absurd h' hy1
  · rintro rfl; exact Moves.perm (List.Perm.refl _)

/-- **The conjecture fails in every degree `d ≥ 2`.** -/
theorem not_conjectureInDegree (s : ℂ) (hs : s ≠ 0) (d : ℕ) (hd : 2 ≤ d) :
    ¬ ConjectureInDegree s d := by
  intro H
  have h := H (fam s 2 (d - 2)) (fam s 3 (d - 2)) (fam_isEigensystem s hs 2 _ le_rfl)
    (fam_isEigensystem s hs 3 _ (by norm_num)) (by simp [fam]; omega) (by simp [fam]; omega)
    (by rw [fam_sign s hs 2 _ le_rfl, fam_sign s hs 3 _ (by norm_num)])
  have := (fam_moves_iff s hs 2 3 (d - 2) le_rfl (by norm_num)).1 h
  omega

/-- A singleton eigensystem is `[s]` or `[-s]`. -/
lemma singleton_eigen {s a : ℂ} (h : IsEigensystem s [a]) : a = s ∨ a = -s := by
  have ha := h.1 a (by simp)
  have hp := h.2
  simp only [List.map_cons, List.map_nil] at hp
  have : dual s a = a := by simpa using hp
  exact (dual_eq_self_iff ha).1 this

/-- **The conjecture holds in degrees `0` and `1`.** -/
theorem conjectureInDegree_le_one (s : ℂ) (hs : s ≠ 0) (d : ℕ) (hd : d ≤ 1) :
    ConjectureInDegree s d := by
  intro l l' hl hl' hld hld' hsign
  have hsn : s ≠ -s := fun h => hs (by linear_combination h / 2)
  rcases Nat.le_one_iff_eq_zero_or_eq_one.1 hd with rfl | rfl
  · rw [List.length_eq_zero_iff.1 hld, List.length_eq_zero_iff.1 hld']
    exact Moves.perm (List.Perm.refl _)
  · obtain ⟨a, rfl⟩ := List.length_eq_one_iff.1 hld
    obtain ⟨b, rfl⟩ := List.length_eq_one_iff.1 hld'
    have hpar := (sign_eq_sign_iff s hs _ _ hl hl').1 hsign
    have hab : a = b := by
      rcases singleton_eigen hl with rfl | rfl <;> rcases singleton_eigen hl' with rfl | rfl
      · rfl
      · simp [negFix, hsn] at hpar
      · simp [negFix, hsn] at hpar
      · rfl
    subst hab
    exact Moves.perm (List.Perm.refl _)

/-- **Exact boundary of the conjecture.**  Completeness of the moves holds in
degree `d` if and only if `d ≤ 1`. -/
theorem conjectureInDegree_iff (s : ℂ) (hs : s ≠ 0) (d : ℕ) :
    ConjectureInDegree s d ↔ d ≤ 1 := by
  constructor
  · intro H
    by_contra h
    exact not_conjectureInDegree s hs d (by omega) H
  · exact conjectureInDegree_le_one s hs d

/-- **Completeness for core-free eigensystems of even degree.**  If all
eigenvalues are `±√Q` and the common degree is even, equal sign implies
move-equivalence. -/
theorem complete_coreFree_even (s : ℂ) (hs : s ≠ 0) (l l' : List ℂ)
    (hl : ∀ a ∈ l, a = s ∨ a = -s) (hl' : ∀ a ∈ l', a = s ∨ a = -s)
    (hlen : l.length = l'.length) (he : l.length % 2 = 0) (hsign : sign s l = sign s l') :
    Moves s l l' := by
  have eig : ∀ L : List ℂ, (∀ a ∈ L, a = s ∨ a = -s) → IsEigensystem s L := by
    intro L hL
    refine ⟨fun a ha => ?_, ?_⟩
    · rcases hL a ha with rfl | rfl
      · exact hs
      · exact neg_ne_zero.2 hs
    · have : L.map (dual s) = L := by
        conv_rhs => rw [← List.map_id L]
        apply List.map_congr_left
        intro a ha
        rcases hL a ha with rfl | rfl
        · exact dual_self_s _ hs
        · exact dual_self_neg_s s hs
      rw [this]
  have hpar := (sign_eq_sign_iff s hs l l' (eig l hl) (eig l' hl')).1 hsign
  have hcore : ∀ L : List ℂ, (∀ a ∈ L, a = s ∨ a = -s) → (coreList s L).length = 0 := by
    intro L hL
    rw [List.length_eq_zero_iff, coreList, List.filter_eq_nil_iff]
    intro a ha
    rcases hL a ha with rfl | rfl <;> simp
  have e1 := length_eq_counts s hs l
  have e2 := length_eq_counts s hs l'
  rw [hcore l hl] at e1
  rw [hcore l' hl'] at e2
  unfold negFix at hpar
  rw [moves_iff s hs]
  refine Or.inr ⟨he, Or.inl ⟨fun x h1 h2 => ?_, by omega, by omega⟩⟩
  rw [List.count_eq_zero_of_not_mem (fun hx => (hl' x hx).elim h1 h2),
    List.count_eq_zero_of_not_mem (fun hx => (hl x hx).elim h1 h2)]

/-- **Core-free counterexample in odd degree.**  `[s, s, s]` and `[s, -s, -s]`
are eigensystems of degree `3` with the same sign `+1`, but are not
move-equivalent (in odd degree the number of `+Q` fixed points is invariant). -/
theorem coreFree_odd_counterexample (s : ℂ) (hs : s ≠ 0) :
    IsEigensystem s [s, s, s] ∧ IsEigensystem s [s, -s, -s] ∧
      sign s [s, s, s] = sign s [s, -s, -s] ∧ ¬ Moves s [s, s, s] [s, -s, -s] := by
  have hsn : s ≠ -s := fun h => hs (by linear_combination h / 2)
  have hn : -s ≠ 0 := neg_ne_zero.2 hs
  have e1 : IsEigensystem s [s, s, s] :=
    ⟨by simp [hs], by simp [dual_self_s s hs]⟩
  have e2 : IsEigensystem s [s, -s, -s] :=
    ⟨by simp [hs], by simp [dual_self_s s hs, dual_self_neg_s s hs]⟩
  refine ⟨e1, e2, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [sign_eq_sign_iff s hs _ _ e1 e2]
    simp [negFix, hsn]
  · intro h
    have := (h.relO hs (by simp)).2.1
    simp [hsn.symm] at this

end DualityMoves

end

module

public import Catalog.Geometry.DualityMoves.Verdict

/-!
# Repairing the conjecture: dual-pair moves

`Verdict.lean` shows that pair insertions of `-Q` fixed points (plus twists and
permutations) do *not* generate the sign classes in degree `≥ 2`: the core is
invisible to the sign but invariant under those moves.

Here we show the minimal repair: allow insertion/deletion of an arbitrary
*dual pair* `{β, Q/β}` (with `β = -√Q` this is exactly the old `-Q` pair move;
with `β = √Q` it is a `+Q` pair move).  Then:

* `DualMoves.sign_eq`  — the moves preserve the sign;
* `dual_normal_form`   — every eigensystem reduces to `[s]^a ++ [-s]^b`
  with `a, b ∈ {0, 1}`;
* `sign_eq_iff_dualMoves` — **two eigensystems of the same degree have the same
  sign iff they are related by dual-pair moves**, in every degree.

So the functional equation sees exactly (degree, sign), and the invisible part
of the eigenvalue data is generated by dual-pair moves — not by `-Q` pair moves
alone.
-/

@[expose] public section

noncomputable section

namespace DualityMoves

/-- Moves generated by permutations and insertion/deletion of dual pairs
`{β, Q/β}`. -/
inductive DualMoves (s : ℂ) : List ℂ → List ℂ → Prop
  | perm {l l' : List ℂ} : l.Perm l' → DualMoves s l l'
  | insertDual (β : ℂ) (hβ : β ≠ 0) (l : List ℂ) : DualMoves s l (β :: dual s β :: l)
  | symm {l l' : List ℂ} : DualMoves s l l' → DualMoves s l' l
  | trans {l l' l'' : List ℂ} : DualMoves s l l' → DualMoves s l' l'' → DualMoves s l l''

/-- The old `-Q` pair move is a dual-pair move. -/
lemma DualMoves.insertNegPair (s : ℂ) (hs : s ≠ 0) (l : List ℂ) :
    DualMoves s l (-s :: -s :: l) := by
  have := DualMoves.insertDual (s := s) (-s) (neg_ne_zero.2 hs) l
  rwa [dual_self_neg_s s hs] at this

theorem DualMoves.sign_eq {s : ℂ} (hs : s ≠ 0) {l l' : List ℂ} (h : DualMoves s l l') :
    sign s l = sign s l' := by
  induction h with
  | perm hp => unfold sign; rw [hp.prod_eq, hp.length_eq]
  | insertDual β hβ l =>
    unfold sign dual
    simp only [List.prod_cons, List.length_cons]
    field_simp
    ring
  | symm _ ih => exact ih.symm
  | trans _ _ ih1 ih2 => exact ih1.trans ih2

theorem DualMoves.length_mod_two {s : ℂ} {l l' : List ℂ} (h : DualMoves s l l') :
    l.length % 2 = l'.length % 2 := by
  induction h with
  | perm hp => rw [hp.length_eq]
  | insertDual β _ l => simp only [List.length_cons]; omega
  | symm _ ih => exact ih.symm
  | trans _ _ ih1 ih2 => exact ih1.trans ih2

lemma isEigensystem_iff_ms (s : ℂ) (l : List ℂ) :
    IsEigensystem s l ↔ (∀ a ∈ l, a ≠ 0) ∧ (l : Multiset ℂ).map (dual s) = l := by
  unfold IsEigensystem
  rw [Multiset.map_coe, Multiset.coe_eq_coe]

/-- Removing an element together with its dual keeps an eigensystem. -/
lemma isEigensystem_erase_pair {s : ℂ} (hs : s ≠ 0) {l : List ℂ} (hl : IsEigensystem s l)
    {a : ℂ} (ha : a ∈ l) : IsEigensystem s ((l.erase a).erase (dual s a)) := by
  rw [isEigensystem_iff_ms] at hl ⊢
  obtain ⟨h0, hd⟩ := hl
  refine ⟨fun c hc => h0 c (List.mem_of_mem_erase (List.mem_of_mem_erase hc)), ?_⟩
  rw [← Multiset.coe_erase, ← Multiset.coe_erase, Multiset.map_erase _ (dual_injective hs),
    Multiset.map_erase _ (dual_injective hs), hd, dual_dual hs (h0 a ha), Multiset.erase_comm]

/-- If `a` and (another copy of) its dual both occur, split them off. -/
lemma perm_pair {s : ℂ} {l : List ℂ} {a : ℂ} (ha : a ∈ l) (hb : dual s a ∈ l.erase a) :
    l.Perm (a :: dual s a :: (l.erase a).erase (dual s a)) :=
  (List.perm_cons_erase ha).trans ((List.perm_cons_erase hb).cons a)

/-- **Normal form.**  Every duality eigensystem is dual-move equivalent to
`[s]^(a mod 2) ++ [-s]^(b mod 2)`, where `a, b` count the `+Q` and `-Q` fixed
points. -/
theorem dual_normal_form (s : ℂ) (hs : s ≠ 0) : ∀ (l : List ℂ), IsEigensystem s l →
    DualMoves s l (nf s (l.count s % 2) (l.count (-s) % 2) []) := by
  have hsn : s ≠ -s := fun h => hs (by linear_combination h / 2)
  intro l
  induction hn : l.length using Nat.strong_induction_on generalizing l with
  | _ n ih =>
  intro hl
  -- a generic pair-removal step
  have step : ∀ a, a ∈ l → dual s a ∈ l.erase a →
      DualMoves s l ((l.erase a).erase (dual s a)) ∧
        ((l.erase a).erase (dual s a)).length + 2 = n ∧
        IsEigensystem s ((l.erase a).erase (dual s a)) := by
    intro a ha hb
    have hp := perm_pair ha hb
    refine ⟨(DualMoves.perm hp).trans
      (DualMoves.symm (DualMoves.insertDual a (hl.1 a ha) _)), ?_,
      isEigensystem_erase_pair hs hl ha⟩
    rw [← hn, hp.length_eq]; simp
  by_cases hA : ∃ a ∈ l, a ≠ s ∧ a ≠ -s
  · obtain ⟨a, ha, h1, h2⟩ := hA
    have ha0 := hl.1 a ha
    have hfix : dual s a ≠ a := fun h => (dual_eq_self_iff ha0).1 h |>.elim h1 h2
    have hbl : dual s a ∈ l := hl.2.mem_iff.1 (List.mem_map_of_mem ha)
    have hb := (List.mem_erase_of_ne hfix).2 hbl
    have hb1 : dual s a ≠ s := fun h => h1 (by
      rw [← dual_dual hs ha0, h, dual_self_s s hs])
    have hb2 : dual s a ≠ -s := fun h => h2 (by
      rw [← dual_dual hs ha0, h, dual_self_neg_s s hs])
    obtain ⟨hm, hlen, he⟩ := step a ha hb
    have IH := ih _ (by omega) _ rfl he
    rw [List.count_erase_of_ne (Ne.symm hb1), List.count_erase_of_ne (Ne.symm h1),
      List.count_erase_of_ne (Ne.symm hb2), List.count_erase_of_ne (Ne.symm h2)] at IH
    exact hm.trans IH
  push_neg at hA
  by_cases hS : 2 ≤ l.count s
  · have ha : s ∈ l := List.count_pos_iff.1 (by omega)
    have hb : dual s s ∈ l.erase s := by
      rw [dual_self_s s hs, ← List.count_pos_iff, List.count_erase_self]; omega
    obtain ⟨hm, hlen, he⟩ := step s ha hb
    have IH := ih _ (by omega) _ rfl he
    rw [dual_self_s s hs] at hm IH
    rw [List.count_erase_self, List.count_erase_self, List.count_erase_of_ne hsn.symm,
      List.count_erase_of_ne hsn.symm] at IH
    have : (l.count s - 1 - 1) % 2 = l.count s % 2 := by omega
    rw [this] at IH
    exact hm.trans IH
  by_cases hN : 2 ≤ l.count (-s)
  · have ha : -s ∈ l := List.count_pos_iff.1 (by omega)
    have hb : dual s (-s) ∈ l.erase (-s) := by
      rw [dual_self_neg_s s hs, ← List.count_pos_iff, List.count_erase_self]; omega
    obtain ⟨hm, hlen, he⟩ := step (-s) ha hb
    have IH := ih _ (by omega) _ rfl he
    rw [dual_self_neg_s s hs] at hm IH
    rw [List.count_erase_self, List.count_erase_self, List.count_erase_of_ne hsn,
      List.count_erase_of_ne hsn] at IH
    have : (l.count (-s) - 1 - 1) % 2 = l.count (-s) % 2 := by omega
    rw [this] at IH
    exact hm.trans IH
  -- only `±s`, each at most once
  apply DualMoves.perm
  rw [List.perm_iff_count]
  intro x
  rw [count_nf s hs]
  by_cases h1 : x = s
  · rw [if_pos h1, if_neg (by rw [h1]; exact hsn), h1]; simp; omega
  · by_cases h2 : x = -s
    · rw [if_neg h1, if_pos h2, h2]; simp; omega
    · rw [if_neg h1, if_neg h2]
      simp only [List.count_nil, add_zero]
      exact List.count_eq_zero_of_not_mem (fun hx => h2 (hA x hx h1))

/-- **Corrected conjecture (all degrees).**  Two duality eigensystems of the same
degree have the same sign if and only if they are related by permutations and
insertions/deletions of dual pairs `{β, Q/β}`. -/
theorem sign_eq_iff_dualMoves (s : ℂ) (hs : s ≠ 0) (l l' : List ℂ)
    (hl : IsEigensystem s l) (hl' : IsEigensystem s l') (hlen : l.length = l'.length) :
    sign s l = sign s l' ↔ DualMoves s l l' := by
  constructor
  · intro hsign
    have hpar := (sign_eq_sign_iff s hs l l' hl hl').1 hsign
    unfold negFix at hpar
    have r1 := dual_normal_form s hs l hl
    have r2 := dual_normal_form s hs l' hl'
    have p1 := r1.length_mod_two
    have p2 := r2.length_mod_two
    simp only [nf, List.length_append, List.length_replicate, List.append_nil] at p1 p2
    have hpos : l'.count s % 2 = l.count s % 2 := by omega
    rw [hpos, ← hpar] at r2
    exact r1.trans r2.symm
  · exact fun h => h.sign_eq hs

/-- The old moves are strictly weaker: in degree `2`, `[2s, s/2]` and `[3s, s/3]`
are dual-move equivalent (so the sign classes are generated by dual-pair moves)
although they are not related by `-Q` pair moves and twists. -/
theorem dualMoves_strictly_stronger (s : ℂ) (hs : s ≠ 0) :
    DualMoves s (fam s 2 0) (fam s 3 0) ∧ ¬ Moves s (fam s 2 0) (fam s 3 0) := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · refine (sign_eq_iff_dualMoves s hs _ _ (fam_isEigensystem s hs 2 0 le_rfl)
      (fam_isEigensystem s hs 3 0 (by norm_num)) (by simp [fam])).1 ?_
    rw [fam_sign s hs 2 0 le_rfl, fam_sign s hs 3 0 (by norm_num)]
  · intro h
    have := (fam_moves_iff s hs 2 3 0 le_rfl (by norm_num)).1 h
    omega

end DualityMoves

end

public import Mathlib

/-!
# Duality eigensystems and their sign

We model the eigenvalue data of a pure weight-`w` piece of a Weil cohomology
satisfying Poincaré duality.  Write `Q = q ^ w` and fix a square root `s` of `Q`
(so `s ^ 2 = Q`; for an honest Weil number `s = q ^ (w / 2) > 0`, but all the
algebra below works for any nonzero complex `s`).

* A *duality eigensystem* is a finite list of nonzero complex numbers
  `α₁, …, α_d` (the inverse roots of the characteristic polynomial) which, as a
  multiset, is stable under the duality involution `α ↦ Q / α = s ^ 2 / α`.
* Its *sign* is `ε = (α₁ ⋯ α_d) / s ^ d`; this is the sign appearing in the
  functional equation `P(1 / (Q T)) = ± ε Q^{-d/2} T^{-d} P(T)`.
* The fixed points of the involution are exactly `±s`; we call `-s` the
  *`-Q` fixed points* (the eigenvalue `-√Q`).

The main result of this file is the *sign formula*
`ε = (-1) ^ (number of -Q fixed points)`, proved by peeling off fixed points and
dual pairs one at a time.
-/

@[expose] public section

noncomputable section

namespace DualityMoves

open Multiset

/-- The duality involution `α ↦ Q / α`, written with `Q = s ^ 2`. -/
def dual (s a : ℂ) : ℂ := s ^ 2 / a

/-- A *duality eigensystem* (relative to `s = √Q`): nonzero eigenvalues whose
multiset is stable under `α ↦ s ^ 2 / α`. -/
def IsEigensystem (s : ℂ) (l : List ℂ) : Prop :=
  (∀ a ∈ l, a ≠ 0) ∧ List.Perm (l.map (dual s)) l

/-- The sign of the functional equation: `∏ αᵢ / s ^ d`. -/
noncomputable def sign (s : ℂ) (l : List ℂ) : ℂ := l.prod / s ^ l.length

/-- Number of `-Q` fixed points, i.e. occurrences of the eigenvalue `-s`. -/
def negFix (s : ℂ) (l : List ℂ) : ℕ := l.count (-s)

lemma dual_injective {s : ℂ} (hs : s ≠ 0) : Function.Injective (dual s) := by
  intro a b h
  unfold dual at h
  have hs2 : s ^ 2 ≠ 0 := pow_ne_zero 2 hs
  rw [div_eq_mul_inv, div_eq_mul_inv] at h
  exact inv_injective (mul_left_cancel₀ hs2 h)

lemma dual_dual {s a : ℂ} (hs : s ≠ 0) (ha : a ≠ 0) : dual s (dual s a) = a := by
  unfold dual; field_simp

lemma dual_neg (s a : ℂ) : dual s (-a) = - dual s a := by
  unfold dual; ring

lemma dual_ne_zero {s a : ℂ} (hs : s ≠ 0) (ha : a ≠ 0) : dual s a ≠ 0 := by
  unfold dual; exact div_ne_zero (pow_ne_zero 2 hs) ha

/-- The fixed points of the duality involution are exactly `±s`. -/
lemma dual_eq_self_iff {s a : ℂ} (ha : a ≠ 0) : dual s a = a ↔ a = s ∨ a = -s := by
  unfold dual
  rw [div_eq_iff ha]
  constructor
  · intro h
    have : (a - s) * (a + s) = 0 := by linear_combination -h
    rcases mul_eq_zero.1 this with h1 | h1
    · left; linear_combination h1
    · right; linear_combination h1
  · rintro (rfl | rfl) <;> ring

lemma dual_self_s (s : ℂ) (hs : s ≠ 0) : dual s s = s :=
  (dual_eq_self_iff hs).2 (Or.inl rfl)

lemma dual_self_neg_s (s : ℂ) (hs : s ≠ 0) : dual s (-s) = -s :=
  (dual_eq_self_iff (neg_ne_zero.2 hs)).2 (Or.inr rfl)

/-- Removing one element `a` from a duality-closed multiset: the result is closed
under duality after also removing `dual a`. -/
lemma map_dual_erase {s : ℂ} (hs : s ≠ 0) (M : Multiset ℂ) (hM : M.map (dual s) = M)
    (a : ℂ) : (M.erase a).map (dual s) = M.erase (dual s a) := by
  rw [Multiset.map_erase _ (dual_injective hs), hM]

/-- **Sign formula (multiset form).**  For a duality-closed multiset of nonzero
numbers, `∏ α = (-1) ^ #{α = -s} · s ^ d`. -/
theorem prod_eq_of_dualClosed {s : ℂ} (hs : s ≠ 0) :
    ∀ (M : Multiset ℂ), (∀ a ∈ M, a ≠ 0) → M.map (dual s) = M →
      M.prod = (-1) ^ (M.count (-s)) * s ^ (card M) := by
  intro M
  induction hn : card M using Nat.strong_induction_on generalizing M with
  | _ n ih =>
  intro h0 hd
  rcases Multiset.empty_or_exists_mem M with rfl | ⟨a, haM⟩
  · subst hn; simp
  have ha0 := h0 a haM
  have hsn : s ≠ -s := fun h => hs (by linear_combination h / 2)
  by_cases hfix : dual s a = a
  · -- a is a fixed point: a = s or a = -s
    set M' := M.erase a with hM'
    have hM : M = a ::ₘ M' := (Multiset.cons_erase haM).symm
    have h0' : ∀ b ∈ M', b ≠ 0 := fun b hb => h0 b (Multiset.mem_of_mem_erase hb)
    have hd' : M'.map (dual s) = M' := by
      have := map_dual_erase hs M hd a
      rwa [hfix] at this
    have hcard : card M' + 1 = n := by rw [← hn, hM, Multiset.card_cons]
    have IH := ih (card M') (by omega) M' rfl h0' hd'
    rw [hM, Multiset.prod_cons, IH, ← hcard]
    rcases (dual_eq_self_iff ha0).1 hfix with rfl | rfl
    · rw [Multiset.count_cons_of_ne hsn.symm]; ring
    · rw [Multiset.count_cons_self]; ring
  · -- a is paired with b = dual a ≠ a
    set b := dual s a with hb
    have hbM : b ∈ M := by rw [← hd]; exact Multiset.mem_map_of_mem _ haM
    have hbM' : b ∈ M.erase a := (Multiset.mem_erase_of_ne hfix).2 hbM
    set M'' := (M.erase a).erase b with hM''
    have hM : M = a ::ₘ b ::ₘ M'' := by
      rw [hM'', Multiset.cons_erase hbM', Multiset.cons_erase haM]
    have h0' : ∀ c ∈ M'', c ≠ 0 := fun c hc =>
      h0 c (Multiset.mem_of_mem_erase (Multiset.mem_of_mem_erase hc))
    have hd' : M''.map (dual s) = M'' := by
      rw [hM'', Multiset.map_erase _ (dual_injective hs), map_dual_erase hs M hd a,
        hb, dual_dual hs ha0, Multiset.erase_comm]
    have hcard : card M'' + 2 = n := by rw [← hn, hM]; simp
    have IH := ih (card M'') (by omega) M'' rfl h0' hd'
    have ha_ne : a ≠ -s := fun h => hfix (by rw [hb, h]; exact dual_self_neg_s s hs)
    have hb_ne : b ≠ -s := by
      intro h
      apply ha_ne
      have : dual s b = dual s (-s) := by rw [h]
      rwa [hb, dual_dual hs ha0, dual_self_neg_s s hs] at this
    have hab : a * b = s ^ 2 := by rw [hb]; unfold dual; field_simp
    rw [hM, Multiset.prod_cons, Multiset.prod_cons, ← mul_assoc, hab, IH,
      Multiset.count_cons_of_ne ha_ne.symm, Multiset.count_cons_of_ne hb_ne.symm, ← hcard]
    ring

/-- **Sign formula.**  For every duality eigensystem,
`∏ αᵢ = (-1) ^ (#-Q fixed points) · s ^ d`. -/
theorem prod_eq (s : ℂ) (hs : s ≠ 0) (l : List ℂ) (hl : IsEigensystem s l) :
    l.prod = (-1) ^ negFix s l * s ^ l.length := by
  have hd : (l : Multiset ℂ).map (dual s) = l := by
    rw [Multiset.map_coe]; exact Multiset.coe_eq_coe.2 hl.2
  have := prod_eq_of_dualClosed hs (l : Multiset ℂ) (fun a ha => hl.1 a ha) hd
  simpa [negFix] using this

/-- **Sign formula.**  The sign of a duality eigensystem is
`(-1) ^ (number of -Q fixed points)`. -/
theorem sign_eq (s : ℂ) (hs : s ≠ 0) (l : List ℂ) (hl : IsEigensystem s l) :
    sign s l = (-1) ^ negFix s l := by
  rw [sign, prod_eq s hs l hl, mul_div_assoc, div_self (pow_ne_zero _ hs), mul_one]

/-- Two duality eigensystems have the same sign iff their numbers of `-Q` fixed
points have the same parity (the "proved converse" in sign-parity form). -/
theorem sign_eq_sign_iff (s : ℂ) (hs : s ≠ 0) (l l' : List ℂ)
    (hl : IsEigensystem s l) (hl' : IsEigensystem s l') :
    sign s l = sign s l' ↔ negFix s l % 2 = negFix s l' % 2 := by
  rw [sign_eq s hs l hl, sign_eq s hs l' hl']
  rcases Nat.even_or_odd (negFix s l) with h1 | h1 <;>
    rcases Nat.even_or_odd (negFix s l') with h2 | h2 <;>
    simp [h1.neg_one_pow, h2.neg_one_pow, Nat.even_iff.1, Nat.odd_iff.1, h1, h2] <;>
    norm_num

end DualityMoves

end

module

public import Catalog.Geometry.DualityMoves.Basic

/-!
# The move relation on eigensystems

We formalise the moves of the conjecture as an inductive relation on lists of
eigenvalues:

* `perm`       — reorder the eigenvalues;
* `insertPair` — insert a pair of `-Q` fixed points `-s, -s` (and, through
  `symm`, delete such a pair);
* `twist`      — the quadratic twist `α ↦ -α` (the only twists preserving
  duality are by `±1`); it changes the sign by `(-1)^d`, so it is a
  sign-preserving move exactly in even degree, which is when we allow it;
* `symm`, `trans` — the relation is the equivalence relation generated.

Main results:
* `Moves.sign_eq`        — the moves preserve the sign (sign invariance);
* `Moves.isEigensystem`  — the moves preserve being a duality eigensystem;
* `Moves.length_mod_two` — degree parity is preserved;
* `Moves.relR`, `Moves.relO` — the finer invariants preserved by the moves.
-/

@[expose] public section

noncomputable section

namespace DualityMoves

/-- The move relation generated by permutations, insertion/deletion of a pair
of `-Q` fixed points, and (sign-preserving, i.e. even-degree) quadratic twists. -/
inductive Moves (s : ℂ) : List ℂ → List ℂ → Prop
  | perm {l l' : List ℂ} : l.Perm l' → Moves s l l'
  | insertPair (l : List ℂ) : Moves s l (-s :: -s :: l)
  | twist (l : List ℂ) : Even l.length → Moves s l (l.map Neg.neg)
  | symm {l l' : List ℂ} : Moves s l l' → Moves s l' l
  | trans {l l' l'' : List ℂ} : Moves s l l' → Moves s l' l'' → Moves s l l''

/-- The *core* of an eigenvalue list: the eigenvalues that are not fixed by
duality (everything except `±s`). -/
def coreList (s : ℂ) (l : List ℂ) : List ℂ := l.filter (fun a => decide (a ≠ s ∧ a ≠ -s))

/-- The core as a multiset (order forgotten). -/
def core (s : ℂ) (l : List ℂ) : Multiset ℂ := (coreList s l : Multiset ℂ)

lemma count_coreList (s x : ℂ) (l : List ℂ) :
    (coreList s l).count x = if x ≠ s ∧ x ≠ -s then l.count x else 0 := by
  unfold coreList
  split_ifs with h
  · exact List.count_filter (by simpa using h)
  · apply List.count_eq_zero_of_not_mem
    intro hx
    rw [List.mem_filter] at hx
    exact h (by simpa using hx.2)

lemma core_eq_iff (s : ℂ) (l l' : List ℂ) :
    core s l = core s l' ↔ ∀ x, x ≠ s → x ≠ -s → l.count x = l'.count x := by
  unfold core
  rw [Multiset.coe_eq_coe, List.perm_iff_count]
  constructor
  · intro h x h1 h2
    have := h x
    rwa [count_coreList, count_coreList, if_pos ⟨h1, h2⟩, if_pos ⟨h1, h2⟩] at this
  · intro h x
    rw [count_coreList, count_coreList]
    split_ifs with h'
    · exact h x h'.1 h'.2
    · rfl

lemma count_map_neg (x : ℂ) (l : List ℂ) : (l.map Neg.neg).count x = l.count (-x) := by
  have := List.count_map_of_injective l Neg.neg neg_injective (-x)
  simpa using this

lemma core_map_neg (s : ℂ) (l : List ℂ) :
    core s (l.map Neg.neg) = (core s l).map Neg.neg := by
  unfold core
  rw [Multiset.map_coe, Multiset.coe_eq_coe, List.perm_iff_count]
  intro x
  rw [count_coreList, count_map_neg, count_map_neg, count_coreList]
  have : (x ≠ s ∧ x ≠ -s) ↔ (-x ≠ s ∧ -x ≠ -s) := by
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩
      exact ⟨fun h => h2 (by linear_combination -h), fun h => h1 (by linear_combination -h)⟩
    · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩
      exact ⟨fun h => h2 (by linear_combination -h), fun h => h1 (by linear_combination -h)⟩
  simp only [this]

/-! ### Invariants -/

/-- The invariant preserved by all moves: the core is preserved up to the
twist `α ↦ -α`, and the parities of the numbers of `+Q` and `-Q` fixed points
are preserved (swapped, together with negating the core, by a twist). -/
def RelR (s : ℂ) (l l' : List ℂ) : Prop :=
  ((∀ x, x ≠ s → x ≠ -s → l'.count x = l.count x) ∧
      l'.count s % 2 = l.count s % 2 ∧ l'.count (-s) % 2 = l.count (-s) % 2) ∨
  ((∀ x, x ≠ s → x ≠ -s → l'.count x = l.count (-x)) ∧
      l'.count s % 2 = l.count (-s) % 2 ∧ l'.count (-s) % 2 = l.count s % 2)

/-- The invariant preserved by moves out of an odd-degree list: the core and the
exact number of `+Q` fixed points are preserved, and the number of `-Q` fixed
points is preserved modulo `2`. -/
def RelO (s : ℂ) (l l' : List ℂ) : Prop :=
  (∀ x, x ≠ s → x ≠ -s → l'.count x = l.count x) ∧
    l'.count s = l.count s ∧ l'.count (-s) % 2 = l.count (-s) % 2

lemma neg_ne_pm {s x : ℂ} (h1 : x ≠ s) (h2 : x ≠ -s) : -x ≠ s ∧ -x ≠ -s :=
  ⟨fun h => h2 (by linear_combination -h), fun h => h1 (by linear_combination -h)⟩

lemma relR_refl (s : ℂ) (l : List ℂ) : RelR s l l := Or.inl ⟨fun _ _ _ => rfl, rfl, rfl⟩

lemma relR_symm {s : ℂ} {l l' : List ℂ} (h : RelR s l l') : RelR s l' l := by
  rcases h with ⟨h1, h2, h3⟩ | ⟨h1, h2, h3⟩
  · exact Or.inl ⟨fun x a b => (h1 x a b).symm, h2.symm, h3.symm⟩
  · refine Or.inr ⟨fun x a b => ?_, h3.symm, h2.symm⟩
    obtain ⟨a', b'⟩ := neg_ne_pm a b
    rw [h1 (-x) a' b', neg_neg]

lemma relR_trans {s : ℂ} {l l' l'' : List ℂ} (h : RelR s l l') (h' : RelR s l' l'') :
    RelR s l l'' := by
  rcases h with ⟨h1, h2, h3⟩ | ⟨h1, h2, h3⟩ <;> rcases h' with ⟨k1, k2, k3⟩ | ⟨k1, k2, k3⟩
  · exact Or.inl ⟨fun x a b => by rw [k1 x a b, h1 x a b], by omega, by omega⟩
  · refine Or.inr ⟨fun x a b => ?_, by omega, by omega⟩
    obtain ⟨a', b'⟩ := neg_ne_pm a b
    rw [k1 x a b, h1 (-x) a' b']
  · exact Or.inr ⟨fun x a b => by rw [k1 x a b, h1 x a b], by omega, by omega⟩
  · refine Or.inl ⟨fun x a b => ?_, by omega, by omega⟩
    obtain ⟨a', b'⟩ := neg_ne_pm a b
    rw [k1 x a b, h1 (-x) a' b', neg_neg]

lemma relO_symm {s : ℂ} {l l' : List ℂ} (h : RelO s l l') : RelO s l' l :=
  ⟨fun x a b => (h.1 x a b).symm, h.2.1.symm, h.2.2.symm⟩

lemma relO_trans {s : ℂ} {l l' l'' : List ℂ} (h : RelO s l l') (h' : RelO s l' l'') :
    RelO s l l'' :=
  ⟨fun x a b => by rw [h'.1 x a b, h.1 x a b], by rw [h'.2.1, h.2.1], by rw [h'.2.2, h.2.2]⟩

lemma count_pair (s x : ℂ) (l : List ℂ) :
    (-s :: -s :: l).count x = l.count x + if x = -s then 2 else 0 := by
  by_cases h : x = -s
  · subst h; simp
  · rw [List.count_cons, List.count_cons]
    simp [Ne.symm h, h]

/-- Moves preserve the parity of the degree. -/
theorem Moves.length_mod_two {s : ℂ} {l l' : List ℂ} (h : Moves s l l') :
    l.length % 2 = l'.length % 2 := by
  induction h with
  | perm hp => rw [hp.length_eq]
  | insertPair l => simp only [List.length_cons]; omega
  | twist l _ => simp
  | symm _ ih => exact ih.symm
  | trans _ _ ih1 ih2 => exact ih1.trans ih2

/-- All moves preserve the invariant `RelR`. -/
theorem Moves.relR {s : ℂ} (hs : s ≠ 0) {l l' : List ℂ} (h : Moves s l l') : RelR s l l' := by
  have hsn : s ≠ -s := fun h => hs (by linear_combination h / 2)
  induction h with
  | perm hp =>
    have := List.perm_iff_count.1 hp
    exact Or.inl ⟨fun x _ _ => (this x).symm, by rw [this], by rw [this]⟩
  | insertPair l =>
    refine Or.inl ⟨fun x _ b => ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · rw [count_pair, if_neg b, add_zero]
    · rw [count_pair, if_neg hsn, add_zero]
    · rw [count_pair, if_pos rfl]; omega
  | twist l _ =>
    refine Or.inr ⟨fun x _ _ => count_map_neg x l, ?_, ?_⟩
    · rw [count_map_neg]
    · rw [count_map_neg, neg_neg]
  | symm _ ih => exact relR_symm ih
  | trans _ _ ih1 ih2 => exact relR_trans ih1 ih2

/-- Moves out of an odd-degree list preserve the finer invariant `RelO`. -/
theorem Moves.relO {s : ℂ} (hs : s ≠ 0) {l l' : List ℂ} (h : Moves s l l') :
    l.length % 2 = 1 → RelO s l l' := by
  have hsn : s ≠ -s := fun h => hs (by linear_combination h / 2)
  induction h with
  | perm hp =>
    intro _
    have := List.perm_iff_count.1 hp
    exact ⟨fun x _ _ => (this x).symm, by rw [this], by rw [this]⟩
  | insertPair l =>
    intro _
    refine ⟨fun x _ b => ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · rw [count_pair, if_neg b, add_zero]
    · rw [count_pair, if_neg hsn, add_zero]
    · rw [count_pair, if_pos rfl]; omega
  | twist l he =>
    intro ho
    exact absurd ho (by rw [Nat.even_iff.1 he]; omega)
  | symm h ih =>
    intro ho
    exact relO_symm (ih (by rw [h.length_mod_two]; exact ho))
  | trans h1 _ ih1 ih2 =>
    intro ho
    exact relO_trans (ih1 ho) (ih2 (by rw [← h1.length_mod_two]; exact ho))

lemma prod_map_neg (l : List ℂ) : (l.map Neg.neg).prod = (-1) ^ l.length * l.prod := by
  induction l with
  | nil => simp
  | cons a t ih =>
    simp only [List.map_cons, List.prod_cons, List.length_cons, ih]
    ring

/-- **Sign invariance.**  Every move preserves the sign `∏ αᵢ / s ^ d`
(this holds for arbitrary eigenvalue lists, not only eigensystems). -/
theorem Moves.sign_eq {s : ℂ} (hs : s ≠ 0) {l l' : List ℂ} (h : Moves s l l') :
    sign s l = sign s l' := by
  induction h with
  | perm hp => unfold sign; rw [hp.prod_eq, hp.length_eq]
  | insertPair l =>
    unfold sign
    simp only [List.prod_cons, List.length_cons]
    field_simp
    ring
  | twist l he =>
    unfold sign
    rw [List.length_map, prod_map_neg, he.neg_one_pow, one_mul]
  | symm _ ih => exact ih.symm
  | trans _ _ ih1 ih2 => exact ih1.trans ih2

/-- Moves preserve being a duality eigensystem. -/
theorem Moves.isEigensystem {s : ℂ} (hs : s ≠ 0) {l l' : List ℂ} (h : Moves s l l') :
    IsEigensystem s l ↔ IsEigensystem s l' := by
  induction h with
  | perm hp =>
    unfold IsEigensystem
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨h0, hd⟩
      exact ⟨fun a ha => h0 a (hp.symm.mem_iff.1 ha), ((hp.map _).symm.trans hd).trans hp⟩
    · rintro ⟨h0, hd⟩
      exact ⟨fun a ha => h0 a (hp.mem_iff.1 ha), ((hp.map _).trans hd).trans hp.symm⟩
  | insertPair l =>
    unfold IsEigensystem
    have hn : -s ≠ 0 := neg_ne_zero.2 hs
    simp only [List.mem_cons, List.map_cons, dual_self_neg_s s hs]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨h0, hd⟩
      exact ⟨by rintro a (rfl | rfl | ha) <;> [exact hn; exact hn; exact h0 a ha],
        (hd.cons _).cons _⟩
    · rintro ⟨h0, hd⟩
      exact ⟨fun a ha => h0 a (Or.inr (Or.inr ha)), (hd.cons_inv).cons_inv⟩
  | twist l _ =>
    unfold IsEigensystem
    have hmap : (l.map Neg.neg).map (dual s) = ((l.map (dual s)).map Neg.neg) := by
      simp [List.map_map, Function.comp_def, dual_neg]
    rw [hmap]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨h0, hd⟩
      refine ⟨fun a ha => ?_, hd.map _⟩
      obtain ⟨b, hb, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.1 ha
      exact neg_ne_zero.2 (h0 b hb)
    · rintro ⟨h0, hd⟩
      refine ⟨fun a ha => ?_, ?_⟩
      · exact neg_ne_zero.1 (h0 (-a) (List.mem_map.2 ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩))
      · have := hd.map Neg.neg
        simpa [List.map_map, Function.comp_def] using this
  | symm _ ih => exact ih.symm
  | trans _ _ ih1 ih2 => exact ih1.trans ih2

end DualityMoves

end
